Did\nRead the detector writer: tool-latency-budget.ts flags projected tools with effect=write, non-idempotent completion, and no abortCompletionReceipt when measured p95 exceeds 80% of the effective dispatch timeout; the SQL in watchdog.ts includes only positive-duration ok/error/timeout rows. testing:run is effect=write, declares no abortCompletionReceipt, and has a 900s max with a foreground timeout cap. An exhaustive partition of the papercusp-workspace testing:run invocation rows in the last 24h totaled 1,821 calls; 81 rows had status=timeout, error_code=timeout, and the exact `handler returned but signal had aborted` phrase (77 below 60s in recorded duration, 4 at/above 60s). No code changes or tests this turn.\n\n## Left\nInspect the writer semantics for tool_invocations.duration_ms and the existing code:run abort-receipt implementation, then inspect testing:run's persisted result shape to choose a safe receipt. The observed timeouts prove late returns, but whether each test-run side effect had already committed is not yet correlated. Preserve the 81-row evidence and don't infer from p95 alone.\n\n## Key insight\nRoot cause candidate: testing:run lacks a per-tool late-completion receipt, so the dispatcher cannot report an authoritative recorded/not-recorded result after abort. This does not yet explain judge reports that describe populated results.\n\n## Left\nDetermine whether historical warned responses were actually classified as unpopulated due to an unrecognized MCP result shape, whether another client-side warning writer exists, or whether reported 'complete payloads' were inferred from tool success rather than inspected body fields. The warning itself therefore does not establish that the current call failed. Its last 256KB contained 591 rows and none of those failure kinds. This suggests the 1h health summary can miss earlier events because readMcpProxyFailureTail scans only a 256KB tail, but verify against a same-snapshot service-health read and its effective log path before calling that proven. So the per-criterion paging contract says the evidence is complete in this page, while the tools:invoke bounded-payload shaper cut ~80% of that same string. Same for fixture-calibration (3565 chars omitted). An auditor trusting evidenceRead.complete would grade from a 800-char fragment. Workaround that works: pass projection:{ pick:['scorecard.criteria[].evidence'] }, which returned the full string. Suspected cause (unconfirmed): evidenceRead.complete is computed before the tools:invoke result-door projection applies its inline budget, so the two layers disagree. Fix direction: either size the criterion page to fit the invoke-door budget, or have the door downgrade evidenceRead.complete to false / set a next offset when it truncates an evidence field. Evidence: its rollout in ~/.papercusp/su-codex-homes/session-34353/sessions/2026/10/06/rollout-...01a111b1....jsonl, plus log/codex-tui.log startup_prewarm WARN lines.\n- accounts:status already reported chatgpt-sub-cli as usageWalled:true / sustainedlyLimited:true, and 6 other codex pool accounts as usageCreditsAvailable:true.\n- Despite that, coord:presence showed the agent 'parked' and loop:status showed rewakeGuaranteed:true / turnsStalled:true. Nothing escalated to the owner or re-routed the agent. Avi noticed it by hand.\n- Census at ~16:09Z: 79 of 81 live Codex su sessions run routing 'default' on that same login. Several had a last turn ending in usage_limit_exceeded (scan in progress; at least 5 at the time of filing).\n\nROOT CAUSE [inferred from the evidence above]: 'default' routing hard-binds the CLI to the box login and never touches the gateway, so the gateway's failover cannot help. capability:launch-agent defaults account to 'default' (\"the gateway is never selected implicitly\"). No detector turns a usage_limit_exceeded wake result into an alert or a re-route. This is the same class as WI-2141080 / WI-2141347 (fixers stuck on the walled local credential), now hitting su sessions.\nRelated trap: accounts:pin { account:'auto' } on such a session returned appliedLive:true, but gateway:owner_report then showed lastRoute:null with zero requests. Before the fix, the focused regression run failed the four new Codex route cases (the two existing pool tests passed), and source inspection showed the handler went from config fetch directly to durable/live pin writes without reading the active launch route. It now resolves the active adv session in the requested workspace, reuses wakeAccountRouteFromArgv, and refuses known default/none/system routes before any gateway request or pin write. Added explicit workspace-query coverage and mocked sync-sse to keep the unit test away from real Postgres. Also verified the existing Codex usage-limit loop recovery path and its recurrence tests.\n\n## Left\nNo remaining implementation work for this item. The earlier carried check claiming EI-25241045216943981 was still assigned is stale: it was released before WI-10006761 was pulled. The fleet mission remains open; next wake must pull only the rev12 lane with scheduler:get_next.\n\n## Key insight\nA dynamic pin cannot change an active CLI that was launched on a gateway-free route. The API must reject that route before reporting success; the UI check alone did not protect direct tool calls. The reset adapter tests passed 16/16 and the exact Cloud integration file passed 13/13, including the reported transition.","distinguishingTest":"Run a controlled unreset-versus-reset pair of independent router mounts with a pending old-router write, then execute the exact existing-workspace cost-review integration journey with the fixture reset in place.","alternativeHypothesis":"The application's cost-review handler or tutorial reducer independently drops the review transition, regardless of prior router mounts.","predictedObservations":{"hypothesis":"Without a reset, the old mount's pending write is flushed through its adapter and the new router stays unchanged; resetting between mounts lets the cost-review journey advance.","alternativeHypothesis":"Queue reset does not change router state, and the exact integration journey still fails at the cost-review transition."}},"checkpointProseSnapshot":"## Did\nThe exact Cloud tutorial integration file passed via Papercusp's focused test router: testing:run runId 30092068-8003-4c6b-a796-efe847bca491, ledger testRunId 20987281; 13 passed, 0 failed. This includes the existing healthy workspace cost-review action advancing to “Wait for a healthy workspace.” The fixture now resets nuqs's module-level update queue between independent router mounts; the earlier registered unit test and this current integration run confirm the mitigation at the reported boundary. Product source remains unchanged.\n\n## Left\nNo product-source fix is justified by this reproduction: the test passes after fixture isolation, so the original failure is consistent with cross-test pending nuqs queue contamination. Shared PG storage still has about 53.6 GB available on / as of 16:41 UTC, so the previously failing 2%/64-GiB-capped headroom guard has adequate capacity. No shared files or volumes were removed. Continue the assigned fleet lane with the next eligible item.\n\n## Key insight\nThe reported 11/12 failure occurred in the existing-workspace transition. Resetting nuqs's module-level update queue between independent router mounts prevents an earlier test router's pending URL write from consuming a later router's setter; the current exact integration scenario now passes.\n\n## Next action\nPull the next item admitted by fleet claim-spec revision 12.\n\n---\n## Did\nReconciled the cold wake; EI-24937591709395249 remains assigned to this session. Inspected the TanStack adapter lifecycle and nuqs global queue. The controlled unreset A/B run (testing:run 8988e390-5481-47e3-8703-ea4bf9cbe2d8) measured that a pending old-router write and a new-router write flush through the old adapter, leaving the new router unchanged. Added NuqsTestingAdapter queue reset before independent mounts in the Cloud integration fixture and a unit regression. The full adapter test file passed 16/16 (run ea8abd5d-4ff1-41bf-8048-05fec1e14714); git diff --check passed. Added guard-rail fact guard-rail:nuqs-global-queue-test-isolation. Product source remains unchanged.\n\n## Left\nThe exact Cloud integration test remains unverified. testing:run 2d1a74df-714e-4fe5-aed9-9918a9561435 exited before collection with no_report at baseline-schema-global-setup.ts:706, which runs assertSharedTestPgStorageHeadroom. The baseline PG volume is under /var/lib/docker on /dev/nvme0n1p2 mounted at /; df showed 2,787,827,712 bytes available against the 64 GiB configured reserve. docker system df exceeded 60 seconds and was interrupted; no files or volumes were removed. The fleet leader received the measurement and test result in coord messages 8ff3d0c7… and df5abd9c…; both required wakes missed with recipient_alive_not_wakeable. Bulk locks:release also left one owned lock active; captured as EI-25537508504487493, then released the remaining integration-test lock via path selector. Consumers of the Docker root space and the lock-release anomaly's cause remain unknown.\n\n## Key insight\nA pending nuqs global-queue flush retains the first mount's adapter and can consume a later mount's setter. Resetting the queue between independent test routers prevents this class of cross-test write loss. This mechanism is measured; its responsibility for the reported Cloud test failure still needs confirmation in the integration run.\n\n## Next action\nAfter shared test-PG headroom is restored or a private test PG is available, run the exact existing-workspace Cloud cost-review integration test. If it still fails after queue isolation, instrument the page review-handler and companion-observation/reducer boundary; keep product source read-only until that measurement distinguishes the cause.\n\n---\n## Did\nReconciled this cold wake and confirmed ownership remains with me. Run 20875558 executed the immediately preceding prerequisite test plus the target existing-workspace cost-review test: 2 passed, 0 failed. This did not reproduce the failure. Source inspection confirms the Cloud test resets fixture data and unmounts React but does not explicitly reset nuqs' module-global throttle queue. Nuqs flushes through the global queue and resets on a successful flush; that does not prove an update remained pending. Consult conv-muxg7ijq-0000-ff73b2e60bfd4a87b94039b216d75168 found no prior evidence and recommended a controlled cross-mount queue probe. No source edits made; temporary file lock was released.\n\n## Left\nThe failure boundary is still unmeasured. The capped prior failure tail showed the guide at Review configuration and cost with 1/6 confirmed, but did not identify whether navigation, the page review callback, or the companion/reducer observation failed. So 497149484242's key access comes from the KEY POLICY, not a grant.\n- No reachable identity can read the key policy: papercusp-ami-publisher, papercusp-automation, papercusp-p012-customer-admin are denied kms:GetKeyPolicy; papercusp-byoc SSO and papercusp-console sessions are expired.\n- aws-ami-release.ts already runs a clean-account launch proof (cleanAccountProof, line ~724) and release A-r62b passed it, so cross-account launch from a key-policy-listed account works.\n\n## Finding (premise corrected)\nThe filed premise 'cross-account launches still fail' is NOT what was measured: they work for 497149484242. A customer account not in that policy gets launchPermission but no key access, and the clean-account proof cannot catch it because the clean account has key-policy access customers will not. Whether the policy names 497149484242 or the whole org o-hh2i8856vo is unknown (needs a key-admin read).\n\n## Left\nDesign (not started): publishPermissions also creates a KMS grant per share account (GranteePrincipal arn:aws:iam::<acct>:root; Decrypt, ReEncryptFrom, CreateGrant, DescribeKey; the release role can CreateGrant), validateInspection checks it, and the clean-account proof runs against grant-only access (clean account removed from the key policy, needs a key admin).
